dispositions.CONFLICTING: The supplied toy assertions conflict; preserve both without inventing a resolution.
dispositions.NOT_IN_INSPECTED_OBJECTS: The toy case text does not address this question. This is scoped absence in the casebook only.
dispositions.SUPPORTED: The stated toy proposition is supported, with no unresolved material relation within that proposition. This is not branch eligibility.
dispositions.UNRESOLVED: A material toy link or interpretation remains unknown or unsupported; retain the missing fact.

instructions: Fill exactly one grouped assertion for each of the seven questions for each case; retain multiple relevant subclaims in its assertion text.
Only supplied line IDs can support findings. List line_ids=[] for NOT_IN_INSPECTED_OBJECTS and explain scoped absence.
For any other disposition cite the lines that support the statement or expose the missing/contradictory link.
Do not infer patient joins, episode transfer, endpoint conversion, eligibility, untouched status, scale or permission.
Unsupported evidence does not become a software defect. Do not mark any actual source or reader approval as passed.
Write peer_material_seen=false only if true; it is a synthetic-process self-report, not authenticated independence.
usability_notes should record ambiguities or difficulty in this form; an empty list is permitted.

questions.question: Which lexical aliases refer to each originating person and what supports each canonical link?
How does each person relate to distinct specimens, assays and exact headers/objects?
Which index episode and components support each selected exposure, specimen and outcome?
What source-supported pre-index/archival/repeat/lesion/assay policy was fixed before outcome-based selection?
What exactly does the native endpoint mean and which same-episode individual assessment supports it?
What exact measurement and processing contract supports this object and proposed branch use?
What originating-family overlap and actual prior use affect protection for this review?
